definition: Broad doctrinal formula stating the impermanent character of conditioned things.
notes: Use this record for the full formula line when the conditioned side of the family is foregrounded explicitly. It keeps saṅkhata tied to impermanence without collapsing back into created-language, and the OSF glossary supports keeping the family in conditioned-language rather than created-language. This gives translators a governed line when the broad conditioned category is the point rather than the more specific saṅkhārā family. **Open question, raised 2026-08-21.** The notes previously said `SN 43.1 anchors the line itself`. That is not true: SN 43.1 defines the *un*conditioned and contains neither `sabbe` nor `aniccā`. Nor does the phrase `sabbe saṅkhatā aniccā` appear anywhere in the canon that this repository can reach -- the canonical line is `sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā` (AN 3.136), which the sibling record `anicca-sabbe-sankhara` already governs. So this record governs an English line built by substituting `saṅkhata` into a formula the texts state with `saṅkhāra`. That may still be wanted as a translator-facing line, but it is a repository coinage rather than a quoted formula, and it should be either merged into `anicca-sabbe-sankhara` or relabelled as a coinage. Left standing rather than deleted, because the choice is editorial, not a citation repair.

context_rules.context: When surrounding prose is more analytic than concrete
context_rules.notes: Controlled alternate for more analytic English.

example_phrases.notes: The canonical line this record parallels. Cited so the record is not left resting on a phrase no text contains; note that the Pali here reads saṅkhārā, not saṅkhatā. See the open question in `notes`.

authority_basis.scope: Supports the canonical formula line itself.
Supports keeping saṅkhata in conditioned-language rather than created-language.

translation_policy.default_scope: Use as the standard rendering when the broad conditioned category is the point of the formula.
translation_policy.when_not_to_apply: Do not replace conditioned with created, and do not use this broader line when the more specific saṅkhārā formulas are actually in view.
translation_policy.drift_risk: Prevents drift between saṅkhata and saṅkhārā in translator-facing formula work.
